\begin{abstract}
Vision--language models (VLMs) such as Vintern-1B have brought strong multimodal
abilities to Vietnamese, but adapting them to a new Visual Question Answering (VQA)
benchmark remains costly: the usual recipe fine-tunes the language model on many
high-resolution image tiles, while task-specific architectures must be trained from
scratch. In this paper, we propose \textbf{ViBridge-VQA}, a parameter-efficient approach
that improves Vintern-1B without updating any of its pre-trained weights. ViBridge-VQA
feeds the frozen language decoder two complementary kinds of visual tokens from a single
image view: \emph{global} tokens, produced by a small trainable bridge from the
\texttt{[CLS]} vector that Vintern-1B discards, and \emph{local} tokens, produced by
Vintern-1B's own pre-aligned projector and pooled to a chosen budget. We treat the
number of tokens as an accuracy--cost trade-off and select it on validation data as the knee of the
Pareto front. On the reasoning-oriented AutoViVQA benchmark, the selected budget of 50 visual tokens
gives two main results. Training only the bridge (1.35\% of the parameters) raises the F1 of Vintern-1B from 17.6 to 54.6, above the published fine-tuned Vintern-1B,
which reads up to 36 times more visual tokens. Training a lightweight decoder
LoRA together with the bridge (1.57\% of the parameters) raises F1 further to 58.2. Local tokens matter far more than global ones, and they also transfer better to unseen Vietnamese VQA datasets than decoder adaptation alone.

\keywords{Vietnamese Visual Question Answering \and Vision--Language Models \and
Parameter-Efficient Learning \and Visual Token Budget \and Generative VQA}
\end{abstract}
